Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service New York NY
717 AM EST Sun Nov 22 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
Special Weather Statement for locally dense fog for northern 
Long Island, NYC metro, S CT, and much of NE NJ and Lower Hudson
Valley until 9 am

Trends in total rainfall continue to decrease with the greatest
amounts continuing to trend eastward.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
1) Locally dense fog possible early this morning. 

2) Low pressure moving up the coast will impact the area with 
rain this afternoon into Monday morning. Localized minor 
coastal impacts are possible due to approaching full moon on 
Tuesday.

3) Another coastal storm is likely from Wednesday night into 
Friday with heavy rain, strong easterly winds, and widespread 
coastal flooding.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
.KEY MESSAGE 1...
Fog, locally dense, will continue through 9 am. Have issued an 
SPS for NYC metro, Northern Long Island, NYC metro, S CT, and
much of NE NJ and Lower Hudson Valley. Visibilities have
improved south of the L.I.E. from the earlier dense fog. 


.KEY MESSAGE 2...
Low pressure several hundred miles off of the Southeast US coast
will move N and slowly intensify as it moves past Cape Hatteras
this morning, then passes very near the area tonight. Most
models as of 00Z have the low moving north and passing along 
the eastern portions of the CWA. This should allow for the axis 
of heaviest rainfall to fall primarily over Eastern LI and SE 
CT this evening into the overnight period. The low will quickly
push northeast with any lingering shower activity ending by
daybreak Monday morning.

Some light rain could arrive as early as late morning or early
afternoon, then rain should pick up in intensity mid afternoon
into the evening, with the rain moderate to heavy at times,
especially for eastern areas.

Total rainfall has continued to trend generally downward,
especially for western areas. Largely 1-2 inches of rain remains
possible for the eastern half of the area with less than an inch
for the western half of the CWA. Extreme western areas may only
end up with a few tenths of rainfall given the current trends in
the low passing east of the area. 

Wind impact is expected to be low, though exact details will depend
on the track of the sfc low. Generally anticipating winds to 
increase out of the E and then NE as the low approaches the 
area with sustained wind 10-15 mph and gusts upwards of 25-30 
mph possible along the coast. There is a very low chance for a 
brief period of gusts 40-45 mph out of the SE-S out east if the 
low tracks close enough to the area, though this will be 
confined largely to the immediate coastline for Eastern LI and 
possibly coastal SE CT.

A minimal coastal flood threat at worst continues for the south 
shore back bays of Nassau County during the Monday morning high tide 
cycle. Minor coastal flooding benchmarks may just be touched at the 
most vulnerable locations. At this point a statement may eventually 
be needed, but if the system trends further east as the guidance has 
been depicting recently, water levels may fall short. The 
progressive nature of the system is another limiting factor. 

.KEY MESSAGE 3... 

Models continue to agree on a potentially large, impactful 
coastal low pressure system impacting the area Wednesday night 
into Thanksgiving Day and Friday. This system has the potential 
to be more impactful regarding wind and coastal flooding than 
the system moving through on Sunday into Monday. This is due to 
a large and strong high pressure system (1040-1045mb) moving 
over the northeast Tuesday into Wednesday before gradually 
moving offshore into Thanksgiving as the potential low pressure 
approaches from the south. A tight pressure gradient between the
systems may result in a period of strong wind gusts. Gusts 
35-45 mph are a possibility sometime Thanksgiving or 
Thanksgiving night. 

Many locations need less than a foot to reach minor coastal flood 
benchmarks due to high astronomical tides associated with the full 
moon on Tue. The way it stands, the current forecast supports 
widespread minor to moderate flooding, perhaps even localized major. 
In addition beach flooding, erosion, and overwash would all be on 
the table. 

Fast flow should limit flooding concerns, but a period of moderate 
to heavy rain is likely on Thanksgiving. 

It is important to note the mid and upper level pattern is complex 
enough where any subtle change can result in large differences in 
intensity, track, and timing. At this time, it is something to keep 
monitoring.

&&

.AVIATION /12Z SUNDAY THROUGH THURSDAY/...
Low pressure approaches from the south through this evening, 
moving east of the NYC metro terminals tonight. 

Areas of fog with LIFR, locally VLIFR, to start should improve
by 13-15z. MVFR should then prevail into the afternoon, but there
is a chance that conditions become VFR for a time late morning 
into the afternoon. 

Rain will develop from south to north this afternoon and
evening. MVFR appears most likely, but some areas of IFR are
possible for Long Island and southeast Connecticut where the
rain could be moderate to locally heavy at times tonight. The
rain will quickly move north and east of the area 06-09z, but
conditions may remain MVFR until day break Monday. VFR prevails
after 12z Monday.

Light NE winds or variable flow early this morning. Winds will
become NE-E into the afternoon around 10 kt or less. Wind will
then shift to the NE-N this evening and tonight as the low
pressure passes to the north and east. The highest chance for
gusts around 20 kt resides east of the NYC metro terminals
and gusts could reach 25 kt at KGON briefly 03-06z. Winds shift
to the NW to WNW after 06z as the low departs with wind speeds 
remaining 10 kt or less.

 ...NY Metro (KEWR/KLGA/KJFK/KTEB) TAF Uncertainty...
Amendments expected for flight categories early this morning 
especially for the timing of improving conditions. 1/4-1/2SM 
visibilities possible through 14z. 

Occasional gusts around 15 kt possible at KJFK and KLGA this
evening.

.OUTLOOK FOR 12Z Monday through Thursday... 

Monday: VFR. W-NW gusts 15-20 kt.

Tuesday-Wednesday: VFR. 

Wednesday night: Mainly VFR. Chance of MVFR and -RA late.
Increasing E-NE winds with gusts 20-30 kt possible.
 
Thursday: Rain, IFR and LLWS likely. E-NE winds potentially gusting 
35-45kt.

Detailed information, including hourly TAF wind component forecasts, 
can be found at: https:/www.weather.gov/zny/n90

&&

.MARINE...
Locally dense fog possible early this morning on LI Sound, LI
Bays, and NY harbor with visibilities 1NM or less at times. Have
issued an MWS through 9 am. Webcams show visibilities are much
higher along the ocean waters so have left them out for now. 

Otherwise, low pressure moving up the coast will likely produce
SCA conditions on the near shore ocean waters by this 
afternoon, and to all waters tonight. Depending on exact low 
track, a very brief period of gale force gusts is possible, but 
given the increasing confidence in an eastward trending low, the
chance of gales has lowered enough to remove the Gale Watch and
extend the SCA. The outer ocean waters will have periods of 
gales, and as such a Gale Warning is in effect for those areas. 

SCA for the non-ocean waters end by Monday morning with residual
hazardous ocean seas likely to persist into Monday night. Only 
a brief lull in SCA conditions is possible on the near shore 
ocean waters for Tue afternoon and night before winds and seas 
ramp up on Wed with the approach of low pressure from the S, 
interacting with strong high pressure to the north to produce 
strong E-NE winds. On the ocean, gusts 25-30 kt likely to return
by Wed afternoon, ramping up to gale force by Wed night and to 
storm force on Thu. Gale force wind gusts should arrive to the 
non ocean waters by late Wed night and continue into Thu. Max 
significant wave heights should ramp up to at least 12-20 ft on 
the ocean and occasionally to 20-25 ft out east, 7-10 ft on 
western Block Island Sound E of Orient Point, and 4-6 ft on Long
Island Sound as well as the entrance to NY Harbor.
